reasoning: The core question — whether reason-before-verdict (CoT) judging genuinely reduces judge bias susceptibility or merely produces post-hoc rationalizations — is directly and repeatedly addressed in published work. "Explicit Reasoning Makes Better Judges" (arXiv 2509.13332) runs essentially the proposed experiment: thinking vs non-thinking judges on small open Qwen models (0.6B-4B), inference-only, measuring robustness/consistency under verbosity bias and other bias scenarios (verbosity consistency 83.48 thinking vs 73.86 non-thinking). "Faithful or Fabricated?" (arXiv 2605.23970) directly tests whether CoT judges rationalize under verbosity/label/confidence-cue perturbations and evaluates structured-CoT mitigation, which is precisely the rationalization-vs-genuine-reduction framing. "The Silent Judge" (arXiv 2509.26072) quantifies authority/"Expert"-provenance bias (+18% verdict shift) and padding, and LessWrong/AF and CoT-faithfulness work already establish that zero-shot CoT can amplify bias. The proposed three bias channels (padding/verbosity, authority framing, position) and the reduce/unchanged/amplify per-channel comparison are all covered; the only minor gap is the exact bundled three-probe ground-truth construction as a single unified study.

evidence.title: Explicit Reasoning Makes Better Judges: A Systematic Study on Accuracy, Efficiency, and Robustness
evidence.summary: Systematically compares 'thinking' (reason-then-verdict) vs 'non-thinking' (direct-verdict) judges on small open Qwen3 models (0.6B/1.7B/4B), inference-only. Finds thinking improves accuracy (+10.5) and robustness to biases, e.g. verbosity-bias consistency 83.48 (thinking) vs 73.86 (non-thinking). Nearly identical setup to the proposal.

evidence.title: Faithful or Fabricated? A Causal Framework for Rationalization Bias in LLM Judges
evidence.summary: Directly tests whether CoT judges produce post-hoc rationalizations vs faithful reasoning by perturbing non-evidential cues (verbosity, confidence/label, authority-style cues) while holding texts fixed. Finds substantial cue-anchored rationalization and evaluates structured-CoT and Proof-Before-Preference mitigations. Addresses the proposal's central 'rationalization vs genuine reduction' question.

evidence.title: The Silent Judge: Unacknowledged Shortcut Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge
evidence.summary: Quantifies authority/provenance framing bias (an 'Expert' label produces ~+18% verdict-shift for GPT-4o) plus padding/verbosity shortcut biases — covering two of the three bias channels in the proposal.

evidence.title: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
evidence.summary: Establishes that zero-shot CoT can make models MORE susceptible to bias and that CoT explanations rationalize biased answers rather than reducing bias — the amplification hypothesis the proposal aims to test is already documented.

evidence.title: Justice or Prejudice? Quantifying Biases in LLM-as-a-Judge
evidence.summary: Comprehensive quantification of LLM-judge biases including position, verbosity, authority, and CoT bias, with bias-probe-style perturbation methodology over ground-truth items — the measurement framework the proposal would build.
